subject: AIC:NA in dsm model with Family quasi poisson

messages.author: f87814d7c9410bb4
messages.subject: AIC:NA in dsm model with Family quasi poisson
parts:
Hello all,

I am running dsm model on line transect data. Code is following:

mod_ndvi <- dsm(count ~ s(ndvi, bs="ts", k=10), hn.modCos$ddf, segdata, obsdata, engine = "gam")

Results and model fit is coming as expected. 

I am trying to get the AIC value for this model using the following code:

AIC(mod_ndvi)

It shows 'NA' in the results.

While I run the same code for a model with the family object: Tweedie, AIC shows up!

Am I missing something with the family object quasi Poisson??

PS: I was going through some literature that suggests quasi Poisson distribution is best suited for GLM regression. Would you please suggest some readings (with fewer technicalities) to understand the concept behind family objects?

Regards
Deepti

Hello Deepi,
 
a short answer is that AIC is not estimated for quasipoisson models, so the program behaves as expected.
 
To find a work-around you can try to search the web for something like "model selection quasipoisson", which is, probably, a reason for your attempts to look at AIC.
 
Regards,
 
Mikhail

messages.subject: Re: AIC:NA in dsm model with Family quasi poisson
parts:
Thank you Eric and Mikhail for the help.

This is to update on this issue. I went through more literature and figure out a manual way to calculate AIC for quasi-poisson models:

mod_ndvi <- dsm(count ~ s(ndvi), hn.modCos$ddf, segdata, obsdata, engine = "gam")

#LOG LIKELIHOOD of mod_ndvi

LL <- logLik(mod_ndvi)

#MODEL DF = no. of parameters (p) = sum of smooth (edf) + parametric (nsdf) terms

p <- sum(mod_ndvi$edf) + sum(b$nsdf)

AIC <- 2*p - 2*LL

I have validated the above formula with those models which were calculating default AIC and found it correct. This is helpful if I want to compare models using different family objects.

Apart from this, calculating c-hat value (overdispersion parameter) helped in model selection.

Now, I am confused with QQ plot of quasi-poisson, negative-binomial and Tweedie family.

--QQ plot of quasi-poisson family shows points away from line while other two seems to do fine. Other model parameters (test statistics, p-values, deviance explained, residual vs predictor variable etc.) are better in case of quasi-poisson model. Would it be a good idea to reject a quasi-poisson model just based on QQ plot and select other family objects??

Also,
--I find concurvity between spatial variable and habitat variable is >0.8. How serious is this for a model? Should I drop one of the variables??

Thanks again.

Deepti Gupta

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] Re: AIC:NA in dsm model with Family quasi poisson
parts:
Deepti, just a brief comment on the quasi-Poisson.  You need to bear in mind that there is no such distribution as the quasi-Poisson.  Instead, the Poisson model is assumed, then a dispersion parameter is estimated, to inflate the variance from the Poisson.  So if you need to resort to quasi-Poisson, it is because the Poisson is a poor fit to your data, so departure from the line in the QQ plot for Poisson is perhaps to be expected.  By contrast, the negative binomial and Tweedie distributions can have variance greater than the mean, so should fit better.

 

Steve Buckland
